title: Celestia Health POC scoping - timeline & milestones
next_steps: Redwood to share POC pricing spreadsheet and Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison
SE to send benchmark harness and runbook for Celestia to run on their sample dataset
Customer to provide 24h of representative traffic logs and sample prompts by 2026-03-09
Schedule kickoff call for 2026-03-11 - Redwood to propose calendar invite
Exchange IAM details and test service account for VPC peering by 2026-03-10
action_items: Maya Chen: Send POC pricing and contract template (due 2026-03-06)
Mark Ruiz: Share benchmark harness (script + instructions) and sample workload config (due 2026-03-05)
Priya Nair: Provide traffic logs, 10 representative prompts, and success criteria doc (due 2026-03-09)
Sofia Ruiz: Provision test VPC and share peering/network contact (due 2026-03-10)
Oliver Park: Schedule mid-point review and exec readout slots (due 2026-03-07)
summary: POC scoping focused on timelines, success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks. Customer requires <200ms p50 generation for summaries at 50 req/s sustained with 2k token context; main concerns are data residency, SSO and audit logs. Proposed 6-week POC with kickoff, access setup, mid-point performance review, and exec readout. Next steps: share pricing, benchmark harness, and exchange network/IAM details.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll just do a quick intros then jump into timelines for the PoC.
[00:12] Priya (Celestia): Thanks, Maya. Quick note - running late this morning so appreciate the time.
[00:20] Mark (Redwood): Hi team, I'm Mark, I'll be SE on this POC, focusing on performance and benchmark setup.
[00:28] Ethan (Celestia): Ethan here, Head of ML, we'll be evaluating summary and classification workloads.
[00:36] Maya: Great, objective today is to agree success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and a milestone schedule - kickoff, access, mid-point review, exec readout.
[00:48] Daniel (Celestia): Sounds good. Our broad success criteria: 1) p50 latency for summary generator under 200ms, p95 under 700ms; 2) semantic quality on our eval set >= baseline model; 3) cost per 1k tokens under budget target.
[01:05] Mark: Okay, helps to be explicit: what's baseline model and current infra?
[01:12] Ethan: We're on a mixed infra: dev uses GCP Vertex with T4s for small tests, prod runs on on-prem VMs with A100s. Baseline is a finetuned Llama-2 variant that we run today.
[01:24] Maya: Cool. For the PoC we'll show both Redwood Hosted path and Dedicated on your A100s if you want - show tradeoffs for latency and cost.
[01:33] Priya: We care about data residency and compliance so private deployment / VPC peering is preferred for prod, but for initial benchmarks hosted is OK if data is scrubbed.
[01:43] Mark: Noted, we'll provide instructions to sanitize logs. We'll also share a benchmark harness that can run either against Hosted API or a local endpoint in your VPC.
[01:54] Sofia (Celestia): What throughput should we size for? Typical peaks are around 60 rps for summaries during morning syncs, sustained 20-30 rps otherwise.
[02:04] Maya: For the POC let's target a realistic but slightly above peak: 50 req/s sustained, 60-70 rps for short bursts. Include both single-request latency and batching throughput tests.
[02:16] Mark: Also include embedding workloads - you'll want vector search performance measured. What's your embedding traffic?
[02:22] Daniel: Search traffic is lower volume - maybe 10 rps - but latency matters for UI.
[02:27] Mark: Ok, we'll include embedding throughput and recall metrics in the harness.
[02:34] Ethan: For sequence lengths, summaries average ~1.2k tokens input, output ~120 tokens; classification prompts ~300 tokens. We sometimes need 2k contexts for long-doc summarization.
[02:47] Maya: Good detail. That impacts models/kernels we'll test - quantized 4-bit on H100/A100 might change latency. We'll recommend profiles.
[02:56] Priya: Security checklist - SOC2 or ISO docs, SSO with SAML, audit logs and KMS for encryption at rest. Also need legal review timelines.
[03:07] Maya: We'll attach our security pack - SOC 2 report, dataflow diagrams, encryption & KMS whitepaper. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC - we can demo in the kickoff.
[03:18] Oliver (Redwood): Also note we can do a limited dedicated pool if you want SLA-like behavior during the PoC - makes benchmarks more stable.
[03:27] Sofia: That may be helpful for mid-point review.
[03:31] Mark: Proposed POC plan (overview): week 0 kickoff & access, week 1-2 baseline benchmarks (hosted and dedicated), week 3 mid-point review & tuning, week 4-5 larger scale runs + stability, week 6 exec readout and handoff.
[03:47] Daniel: So 6 weeks total? Ok. We want a fast mid-point to decide whether to expand.
[03:54] Maya: Yes, 6-week structured POC with clear gating criteria at mid-point: hit p50/p95 targets, quality regression <2% vs baseline on eval set, and acceptable cost delta.
[04:06] Ethan: For quality evaluation we'll provide an eval harness and 500 labeled examples.
[04:11] Mark: Perfect. For benchmarks we'll run: single-token streaming latency, 1-10 batch sizes, burst tests, and sustained throughput at 50 rps for 30 minutes.
[04:21] Maya: Also do a KV cache demo - show how prefix caching reduces repeated token cost for frequent prompts.
[04:27] Priya: You mentioned K-V cash earlier?
[04:29] Mark: Sorry, K-V cache - sometimes the speech recognition in the transcript writes it as cash - we'll provide a doc explaining KV cache and warm vs cold runs.
[04:37] Daniel: Network topology: we need VPC peering and a service account with limited IAM scope. Sofia will own that.
[04:43] Sofia: Yep, I'll set up a test VPC and share the peering contact.
[04:48] Maya: Actionable dates: we propose kickoff on 2026-03-11; SE shares harness by 2026-03-05; customer provides data by 2026-03-09; mid-point review on week 3 around 2026-03-25; exec readout first week of April.
[05:05] Priya: That timeline looks good. Legal will need the contract; can you send a draft?
[05:11] Maya: Yes, we'll send a POC contract + terms this week.
[05:14] Ethan: Benchmarks - will you run tests on both your Dedicated infra and our on-prem A100s?
[05:21] Mark: We can run a matrix: Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool), and your on-prem A100s via Private deployment. For on-prem we need an infra contact and SSH/entitlement to run the harness.
[05:34] Sofia: Typo - that's Sofia.
[05:36] Maya: Thanks - updated.
[05:38] Daniel: Any competitors we should expect? We are also evaluating Anthropic and Bedrock for latency and managed features.
[05:46] Maya: Understood, we'll show comparative numbers where possible, and focus on predictable unit economics and rollout controls.
[05:54] Mark: On metrics we'll collect: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens (est), quality metrics (ROUGE/BERTScore as you prefer), and error/retry rates.
[06:05] Priya: For the exec readout we want a 15-minute summary of runway to prod, costs, and recommended deployment mode.
[06:12] Oliver: We'll prepare a short deck for mid-point and exec readout, with clear go/no-go recommendations.
[06:18] Maya: Any outstanding concerns?
[06:20] Ethan: Data residency + audit logs - need to confirm retention windows and ability to disable logs for sensitive flows.
[06:26] Mark: We support configurable retention and can disable logging for specific routes; we'll capture that in the security pack.
[06:33] Priya: Ok great.
[06:35] Maya: Recap of next steps: send pricing/contract, share benchmark harness, customer to provide logs and prompts, set up VPC peering, schedule kickoff. We'll log action items in CRM.
[06:47] Daniel: Thanks all. Looking forward to the kickoff.
[06:50] Maya: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up by EOD with the calendar and artifacts.
[06:55] [call ends]
